title: Scoped Role Fabric and Delegated Admin Patterns
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and spec for RBAC v2 role model that supports: hierarchical resources, parallel scope anchoring (resource, tenant, environment), delegated admin roles, permission matrix semantics, and tight audit-log context. The goal is to provide a deterministic evaluation order that is cheap to evaluate at runtime, straightforward to migrate existing role bindings to, and compatible with SSO/SAML attribute-mapped assignments for enterprise customers and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical role model spec produced and reviewed by Security and Platform (doc link in links)
Permission evaluation algorithm with complexity analysis (O(#scopes + #policies)) and pseudo-code included
Migration plan that can convert existing rolesets to new scoped bindings with sample scripts and fallback guardrails
End-to-end test harness demonstrating: tenant-scoped deny, resource-anchored allow, delegated-admin inheritance, and audit event payloads with full context
SAML/SSO attribute mapping examples and a stubbed SAML connector in the auth service for testing
Performance benchmark: latency regression <5% on token evaluation for common path, and memory overhead budget <= 15% per auth worker
decisions: Adopt a hybrid model: principal->binding->scope->permission tuples instead of monolithic role blobs to allow fine-grained delegation and partial grants
Scopes will be first-class and typed: {tenant,project,resource,environment}. Evaluation uses most-specific match with deny precedence
Delegated admin is modeled as a role flag on a binding (delegated_admin=true) with explicit allowed sub-scope for escalation. Delegation requires audit-enabled approval flow
Audit events will include binding_id, effective_principal, evaluated_scope, decision (allow/deny), rule_id, and correlation_id for tracing across services
SAML integrations will map NameID and attributes into initial bindings; SCIM will remain the canonical provisioning path for bulk assignments
tradeoffs: Using typed scopes increases implementation complexity but yields clearer UI surfaces and simpler policy authoring for SREs and customers
Deny-precedence avoids accidental privilege escalation but requires careful migration to avoid locking out admins — mitigated via staged migration and emergency break-glass roles
Storing granular bindings increases datastore footprint; we plan to introduce compact serialized cache and eviction to balance performance and cost
permission_matrix_examples: resource:models/model-123 -> scopes: [resource] -> allowed_actions: [read, invoke, update_configuration] -> roles: [model-viewer, model-operator]
environment:prod -> scopes: [environment,tenant] -> allowed_actions: [deploy, rollback] -> roles: [deploy-operator], delegated_admin:true
api_contract_examples: POST /v2/rbac/bindings {principal: 'user:alice', role: 'project-admin', scope: {type: 'project', id: 'proj-42'}, delegated_admin: false} -> 201 binding_id
Audit event JSON: {timestamp, binding_id, principal, effective_roles, evaluated_scope, action, decision, rule_id, trace_id}
migration_plan: Phase 1: read-only analysis pass that computes effective permissions for all admin principals and surfaces conflicts. Phase 2: automated conversion tool to emit new bindings from role blobs with dry-run reports. Phase 3: opt-in rollout per org with telemetry to detect admin lockout risk. Phase 4: global flip with emergency break-glass and rollback script. Provide runbooks and a small migration CLI (prototype linked in links).
saml_and_ssO_considerations: Map SAML attributes to principal and initial bindings: e.g., eduPersonScopedAffiliation -> tenant-admin mapping
Support assertion of 'role' claim for short-lived delegated bindings combined with audit events to capture who granted the transient permission
For on-prem/Private installs, provide a configuration toggle to accept or ignore external assertions for admin-level bindings
Require MFA-enforced flag for any binding with delegated_admin=true when provisioned via SSO
audit_and_observability: All grant/revoke actions will emit structured audit events to the audit pipeline with retention tagging based on org compliance settings
Evaluation logs will be sampled at 100% for allow/deny decisions on admin actions and at 1% for routine reads, with on-demand spike capture
Console will surface last-10-evaluations for a given principal and trace link to request/response logs for incident investigation
Provide an 'explain' endpoint that returns human-friendly rationale for a decision (matched bindings, denies, inherited roles) limited to authorized tracers
ui_and_console_notes: Design will expose scope context in every binding row (breadcrumbs: tenant > project > resource)
Bulk role-assignment will support CSV/SCIM imports and show dry-run conflicts prior to commit
Delegation flows will require reviewer approval when creating a binding with delegated_admin=true, with configurable reviewer sets at org level
performance_and_storage: Auth service will maintain an in-memory compact index keyed by (principal, scope_type) for fast lookup
Introduce a background coalescer that aggregates adjacent bindings for the same principal to reduce evaluation cost
Datastore schema: bindings table with serialized permission bitset; future work to migrate to post-quantized column family for large tenants
